44a82e4e25.q: How did WorkPlay Branding transition from a traditional branding agency to a content creation subscription model?
44a82e4e25.a: WorkPlay started in 2019 as a branding agency offering color palettes, logos, and content creation. When clients came in for the $6,000 branding package, they realized people kept coming back asking for more visual content to post on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. By listening to client demands, the founders realized their sweet spot was visual content, not logos and color palettes, so they shifted to a membership model for content. Around 2022, they made a deliberate decision to focus exclusively on media asset creation, which helped expand the brand by doing one thing really well.

38a1dc9274.q: What is the credit system model that WorkPlay Branding is transitioning to instead of quarterly shoots?
38a1dc9274.a: WorkPlay is transitioning from a four-shoots-per-year model to a credit system that allows clients to book on an hourly basis. This change came from client objections on sales calls where people said they only needed four hours instead of a seven-hour shoot, or wanted to split shoots across multiple days. The credit system is proprietary to WorkPlay Branding and allows flexibility—clients can use three hours on one day and four hours on another, or book anything from a two-hour shoot in New York City to a five-hour shoot in Paris.

3b9dfa2d4d.q: How did WorkPlay Branding identify its unique business mechanism instead of copying industry standards?
3b9dfa2d4d.a: Lyric emphasized not looking at industry norms as a blueprint. Instead, WorkPlay observed that photographers had restrictions around content, but as a content creation company, they saw a bigger vision and ignored photography industry rules. They gave clients everything shot with fast turnaround times, and didn't take inspiration from competitors but rather from other industries like Uber and Dry Bar for scaling. By building within isolation for five years without observing competitor moves, they developed a truly unique mechanism that felt disruptive because it had never been done in the photography and branding industry before.

4074b17669.q: What process does WorkPlay Branding use to identify client needs and objections to improve its service model?
4074b17669.a: WorkPlay identifies its sweet spot by listening to what customers are coming to them for and analyzing what they're objecting to on sales calls. Lyric explained that by being cognizant of ideal clients and listening to their objections to the current model, they can create blueprints for unique offerings. For example, client objections about needing fewer hours than a seven-hour shoot led directly to developing the credit system. The key is having self-awareness around what you're good at and recognizing when ideal clients are asking for things that require a model adjustment.
